headline: Segment strength outweighed by a net-income squeeze
summary_short: Celanese's Q2 2026 GAAP revenue rose 8.7% y/y to $2.75 billion on strength in both segments, but net income fell 36.5% y/y to $125 million and diluted EPS dropped to $1.13 from $1.80, even as management's own adjusted EPS of $2.45 was its best in nearly three years.
summary_long: Revenue grew 8.7% y/y and 17.8% q/q to $2.75B as both segments strengthened: Acetyl Chain net sales rose 19% y/y on vinyl-chain volume/margin gains and temporary China pricing dislocation, while Engineered Materials grew on pricing, mix and medical/electronics platform strength. Gross margin expanded to 22.4% and operating income rose 19.5% y/y to $276M. Pretax income grew just 6.8% as Other Activities' net expense rose to $85M on higher compensation accruals; net income fell 36.5% y/y to $125M and diluted EPS to $1.13, a gap not itemized in this document. Cash fell 22.4% q/q to $1.36B after repaying a $508M bond in June. Q3 adjusted EPS guided to $1.35-$1.75; FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of ~$6.00 held.

drivers.explanation: Acetyl Chain net sales rose 19% y/y and 28% q/q on vinyl-chain volume and margin expansion, aided by temporary China supply disruptions that boosted Western Hemisphere pricing; Engineered Materials grew on pricing (+5% y/y ex-Micromax), mix enrichment, and double-digit growth in medical and electronics end markets.

Gross profit grew faster than cost of revenue (15.5% vs 6.9% y/y), consistent with the release's description of disciplined pricing and mix improvements across both segments outpacing raw-material cost growth.
Margin expansion is arithmetic: revenue grew 8.7% while cost of revenue grew only 6.9%, so gross profit outpaced cost growth.

Engineered Materials adjusted EBIT of $234M and Acetyl Chain adjusted EBIT of $321M both grew on stronger commercial execution; Acetyl Chain results also included about $40 million of acetate-tow equity earnings that resumed in the quarter.

Growth in pretax income lagged operating income because Other Activities reported an $85 million net expense in the quarter, which the company attributes to higher compensation accruals than previously expected, narrowing the gap between segment operating strength and consolidated pretax results.
EPS decline of about 37% closely tracks the 36.5% net income decline, with weighted-average share count nearly flat y/y (+0.5%).
Same drivers as basic EPS: the decline is explained almost entirely by the drop in net income rather than share-count dilution.

The company repaid a $508 million bond due July 19 with cash on hand during June, within the quarter; it also repaid a $400 million bond due August 5 subsequent to quarter-end using further cash on hand.

Decline is consistent with the disclosed bond repayments and the company's stated deleveraging priority, though the release does not itemize the exact maturity reclassified out of the long-term debt balance.
Consistent with the disclosed repayment of the $508 million bond that matured within the quarter.
The $104M q/q equity increase is broadly consistent with the quarter's $125M net income, partially offset by other equity movements (e.g., FX translation, dividends) not itemized in this document.

CEO Scott Richardson cited operating EBITDA growth of more than 20% y/y, calling supply disruptions during the quarter transitory and crediting the flexibility of Celanese's global manufacturing and supply-chain network for capturing the opportunity.
